newsitem.title: USA: Walbro expects improvement in second half.
newsitem.headline: Walbro expects improvement in second half.

text.p: Walbro Corp, which earlier reported lower earnings for the second quarter, said Wednesday it expected results to improve during the next six months.

"We anticipate that earnings will gradually improve beginning in the second half of 1997 as new production contracts begin. As additional new business with increased Walbro content phases in, we are confident that the value of our investment in plants and people will become apparent through improved earnings and continued growth," said L.E. Althaver, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.

The maker of precision fuel systems earned $1.2 million, or $0.14 a share, in the second quarter compared with $4.8 million, or $0.56, in the same period last year. Sales dropped to $153.8 million from $155.1 million.

"Sales of automotive products were down compared with the same period of 1996, reflecting a reduction of vehicle sales in the U.S. during the second quarter," Althaver said. "Automotive shipments were affected by the 29-day strike at Chrysler Corp's Mound Road engine plant. That strike reduced Walbro's sales by approximately $3.6 million in the second quarter, while reducing earnings by approximately $1 million, or $0.11 per share, after all related costs."

An in-sourcing project by a major customer of Walbro continued during the second quarter but has been completed, the company said. In addition, the strength of the dollar hurt profitability of Walbro's European and Japanese operations during the second quarter.
